text:
julia: Heads-up: proposal for handling client-initiated graceful shutdown at the edge — aim is to avoid midstream truncation, prevent duplicate hedging, and keep SLAs intact. Thinking: drain window + optional drain-ack trailer + hedging budget tied to a session-lease.

sam: +1 on the problem, we've seen users hit truncated streams during deploys. How do you envision clients expressing intent to shutdown vs normal cancellation?

julia: two signals: client cancellation (normal) remains Cancellation; client-initiated shutdown is a long-lived intent signal (e.g., connection-level CLOSE_WITH_DRAIN). Practically: client can set `Connection: drain` or send a graceful shutdown frame. Edge treats that as "drain intent" and starts a drain-window timer.

ryan: curious about race with retries/hedging. If edge hedges while upstream is draining, we risk duplicate work or inconsistent responses.

julia: exactly. proposal: attach a session-lease token to each in-flight call. Hedging decisions consult a per-session hedging budget. When a drain intent arrives, edge reduces hedging aggressiveness and prioritizes finishing existing sessions. New requests get shorter hedging windows.

maria: what about long streaming calls? We can't block forever. Do we truncate and emit a special trailer?

julia: for streaming, prefer emit a drain-ack trailer when the server finishes: `grpc-trailer: x-drain-ack=true`. If a connection is force-closed before the stream end, emit a final event in logs and surface a 499-ish metric for client-shutdown-truncated.

sam: can we have the client request a checkpoint before shutdown so the server can resume? like a resumable-token?

julia: resumable tokens are an opt-in expensive feature. For short-term runway (drain window) we rely on checkpoints only for very long lived streams. Default behavior: best-effort finish, then drain-ack; fallback policy: allow client to reissue request with idempotency key + `x-session-lease` to avoid duplicated side effects.

ryan: need concrete semantics for the hedging budget. Suggestion: budget = max_hedges_per_session (default 1) and a time-decayed allowance. When `drain` arrives, set allowance=0 for sessions started after drain, keep allowance for inflight but disallow creating new hedged clones.

maria: add metrics: `edge.drain.started`, `edge.drain.completed`, `edge.drain.truncated`, `edge.session.hedge_denied`. Also surface `x-session-lease` in traces so ops can correlate.

infra-bot: deploy-check report: routing-layer currently supports `Connection: close` only. No API for `Connection: drain`.

sam: implementation notes: 1) extend ingress parser to accept `Connection: drain` or `X-Connection-Intent: drain`. 2) add per-session metadata (session-lease id + hedging budget) in request context. 3) trailer passthrough for `x-drain-ack`. 4) config knobs: `drain_window_ms`, `max_hedges_per_session`, `allow_resumable_tokens`.

julia: design tradeoffs: - longer drain window => fewer truncations but higher tail resource usage. - aggressive resumed tokens => complexity and state. - strict no-hedge-on-drain reduces latency protection for unlucky requests. Need tuning and customer-facing defaults.

ryan: edge cases: multi-tenant upstreams that don't understand drain-ack trailers. We should emit telemetry and fall back to TTL-based cutover. Also ensure that when upstream returns 5xx during drain we don't do blind retries that hide customer errors.

maria: test plan: unit test parser + hedging state, integration test with simulated upstream that responds slowly during drain, chaos test that kills upstream mid-drain and asserts metrics and no duplicate side-effects.

julia: next steps: I'll write a short RFC with proto sketches and config examples. Quick ask: anyone object to `x-session-lease` as the header name? (I prefer short names).

sam: fine with `x-session-lease`. can we use lowercase `x-session-lease` for consistency?

ryan: +1. also include runtime flag to disable resumable tokens for privacy-sensitive accounts.

maria: adding note: docs need to call out how this interacts with clients that terminate TCP vs graceful HTTP close.

julia: thanks — I'll drop the RFC link here when ready and tag infra for parsing and telemetry changes. :mag_right:
